html:
Ludwig van Beethoven was a German composer and pianist, born in Bonn in 1770, who spent his working life in Vienna. His music carried the Classical style of Mozart and Haydn into the Romantic age, and he kept composing after he went deaf.

He moved to Vienna in 1792 to study with Joseph Haydn and soon became famous as a pianist. Aristocratic patrons paid him an income, and he was one of the first composers to live largely by selling his work rather than serving a court or church.

His hearing began to fail in his late twenties. In 1802 he wrote a letter to his brothers, the Heiligenstadt Testament, saying that only his art had kept him from suicide. By the end of his life he was almost completely deaf and talked with visitors through notebooks.

Main works:

  • Nine symphonies. The Third, the Eroica, was first dedicated to Napoleon; Beethoven struck out the name when Napoleon crowned himself emperor. The Ninth ends with a choir singing Schiller's Ode to Joy, now the anthem of the European Union.
  • 32 piano sonatas, including the Moonlight and Appassionata.
  • String quartets; the late ones, written when he was deaf, puzzled listeners for decades.
  • One opera, Fidelio, about a wife who rescues her husband from a political prison.

His music grew larger, more personal and more dramatic than what came before, and it set the model of the composer as a struggling genius. Some 10,000 people are said to have joined his funeral in Vienna in 1827.
sum: Ludwig van Beethoven was a German composer and pianist, born in Bonn in 1770, who spent his working life in Vienna. His music carried the Classical style of Mozart and Haydn into the Romantic age, and he kept composing after he went deaf.
